title: 美元回档：市场交易的已是「果」
description:
一条讲给普通人听的宏观逻辑线：通胀是因，联准会紧缩是果，而紧缩的果又是经济成长放缓。

今年 5 月之前，市场主要在反应「因」；5 月之后，开始反应「果」。最直观的证据就是美元指数从 5 月中开始拉回——按理说欧洲被俄乌战争拖累、中国经济疲软还在封城、日本死守宽松，美元走强本来合情合理。可一旦市场认定美国自己也要放缓，那这个差距就没原本想象中那么大了。外汇市场的叙事，正在从 US exceptionalism 转向 global slowdown。

更有意思的是那个「衰退指标」。2018 年联准会经济学家 Eric Engstrom 和 Steven Sharpe 发过一篇论文，认为华尔街惯用的十年减两年殖利率逆差并不是最好的衰退指标，市场隐含的 18 个月后三月期殖利率减当前三月期殖利率才更准。三月份两年十年倒挂闹得凶的时候，Powell 就是拿这个指标出来说「不用太紧张」。

可现在，连 Powell 自己偏爱的这个指标，都开始往错误的方向走了。

#美元 #衰退 #殖利率倒挂 #联准会 #宏观 #投资

quotes.zh: 市场在今年5月前主要是反应因，5月后开始反应果。
quotes.en: Before May the market was trading the cause; after May it started trading the effect.

quotes.zh: 外汇市场的想法，正在从 US exceptionalism 转往 global slowdown。
quotes.en: The FX market's view is shifting from US exceptionalism toward global slowdown.

quotes.zh: 就连主席 Powell 认为比较好的这个指标，都开始往错误的方向走。
quotes.en: Even the indicator chair Powell considers better has started moving the wrong way.

translations: Put simply, inflation is the cause: it forces the Fed to tighten monetary policy to suppress inflation. And the effect?
Slower economic growth.
Right now it looks like the market was mainly trading the cause before May this year,
but after May it started trading the effect.
In episode 51, released on March 17, we talked about two early indicators of a US recession.
From March until now, the recession question has drawn more and more discussion.
If we look at Google Trends data, searches for that keyword keep climbing,
and plenty of people are asking outright: is the 2022 we are living through a recession or not?
By Bloomberg's count, recent recession-related news has also hit its highest level since the COVID-19 pandemic in 2020.
On top of that, if we look at the dollar index, it has pulled back since mid-May.
Compared with the world's other major economies, Europe is weighed down by the Russia-Ukraine war, China's economy was already soft,
and it is still sticking to zero-COVID and locking down cities.
Japan, meanwhile, is holding on to loose monetary policy. So whether we looked at relative economic strength,
or at the direction of monetary policy, a stronger dollar made perfect sense.
But if the market is now starting to worry that US growth will slow after all, then even though Europe and China may still be worse off,
the gap between them and the US may not be as wide as originally assumed.
Put simply, the FX market's view may be shifting away from the idea that the US will do far better than other major economies this year,
US exceptionalism, and toward the whole world doing merely so-so,
global slowdown.
Everyone has also seen the dollar index post a relatively large pullback, and even the recession indicator favoured by Fed chair Powell
seems to have started moving.
In 2018, Fed economists Eric Engstrom and Steven Sharpe
published a paper arguing that Wall Street's habitual gauge, the spread between 10-year and 2-year US Treasury yields,
is not the best recession indicator. They argued that the spread between the market-implied three-month Treasury yield 18 months out
and today's three-month Treasury yield is a far more accurate recession indicator.
Back in March, when the market was fretting about the 2-year and 10-year Treasury yields inverting,
chair Powell brought out exactly this indicator, saying the spread was the better gauge,
and that it showed no narrowing at all, let alone inversion, so we needn't be too nervous.
But now, even the indicator chair Powell considers better has started moving the wrong way.
It shows that worries about growth really are spreading through the market.
